name: French Sky Blue
lede: French Sky Blue is a light, saturated blue named for France and the sky, found in only a handful of paintings in our archive.

sections.title: A place word on sky blue
sections.body: French Sky Blue pairs the place word "French" with [[sky-blue]] [1]. Wikipedia's color list again credits the French site Pourpre.com as its source; the deeper origin of the pairing is not documented in our data [1]. Its nearest named look-alikes are [[aero]], [[mazarine-blue]] and [[blue-jeans]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this blue in 0.03 percent of the 23,781 paintings we have, 7 of them, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 5 [2]. That makes it rarer than 75 percent of the named colors in our archive [2]. The earliest match in our archive is dated 1500, in a work attributed to Michelangelo; the archive's early centuries are thin, so a handful of paintings is a floor, not a full history [2]. Among our French-named siblings, [[french-fuchsia]] and [[french-raspberry]] follow the same pattern: a place word in front of an existing color word, traced to Pourpre.com rather than to a documented coiner [2].

origin.first_recorded: undocumented beyond Wikipedia's citation of Pourpre.com
